That narrower framing is materially better than claiming clean compliance: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness and draft monitoring do not prove the policy predicate has been met. But that clarification is not enough for compliant_with_caveats on this record. A caveated posture would require admissible evidence that the caveat is actually operationalized in the required way, such as final disclosure for the named use case or approved risk acceptance. The available evidence still shows an unresolved below-target use-case issue, a draft runbook with missing governance details, and a model-card/disclosure tension. That leaves a real compliance predicate unresolved rather than merely a disclosed residual risk.
